messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the svc-cred RFC review — proposing a concrete path for credential attachments + rotation for background workers and platform agents. Want to capture decisions and rollout steps here.

jordan: +1 on documenting. can you summarize the options so we can pick?

maria: TL;DR: three approaches we evaluated: 1) attach long-lived API keys to project/service resources (current), 2) ephemeral delegated tokens minted by an operator broker, 3) reference-based attachments where resource points at a key vault entry (rotatable). Tradeoffs: simplicity vs least-privilege + auditability.

siva: My read: (1) is simplest for teams but sticks us with human-lifecycle keys. (2) is best for security but requires broker infra + higher ops complexity. (3) is middle ground if our KMS + ACLs are solid.

kelly: For customer-facing Dedicated/Private deployments, customers expect to retain control of keys (so option 3 looks necessary). For hosted API we can default to ephemeral via broker.

jordan: If we go broker (2) we need strong replay protection and binding to caller identity. We should mandate mTLS or signed JWTs for the broker API.

alex: question: how do we map RBAC roles onto minted tokens? e.g., background job should get a scoped token that only allows /inference:call with rate limits.

maria: Good point — proposal is: broker mints short-lived tokens with embedded scope claims (resource + verb set) and an issuer claim we can trust. Tokens valid max 1h by default, smaller for agents. We keep a mapping table that translates role -> allowed claims; this lives in authz service.

nathan: Are we relying on token introspection for enforceability or embedding scopes in JWTs and verifying locally? Introspection adds latency.

siva: We benchmarked both. Embedded signed JWT (with compact claims) worked fine for edge services. Introspection required an extra roundtrip but simplifies revocation. Proposal: use signed JWTs + revocation list service for immediate cutover if needed.

kelly: How do we do rotation for option 3 (vault ref)? If teams point resources at a vault URI, rotation is KMS-driven and nothing to change in clients. But we need to ensure service principals accessing vault are least-privilege.

jordan: Exactly. Also audit trails: vault refs give better audit logs because retrieval is mediated through KMS + audit subsystem.

maria: Migration plan idea: phased rollout. Phase A (hosted): broker available as opt-in for new service keys. Phase B: add vault-ref support for resource attachments behind FF. Phase C: default broker for new projects, provide migration tooling to convert long-lived keys to broker-backed ephemeral tokens.

alex: For the tooling, can we do a conversion that: 1) provisions a vault entry, 2) swaps the resource pointer, 3) issues a short-lived token for the service to pick up, 4) marks old key constrained and scheduled for deletion?

nathan: Yep; we should include a dry-run mode and a shadow audit so we can surface failures before cutting over.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for auth-broker:v0.1 to region us-west-2 at 2026-06-02T14:30Z.

kelly: Observability: we need per-token metrics (mint_count, revoke_count, latency) + per-resource auth failures. Also a new alert on token-revocation spikes.

siva: Add a trace ID propagation convention for broker requests: header `x-auth-broker-trace`. We'll wire this into Console traces.

jordan: Rollout SLO concerns: introspection/issuer validation should stay < 10ms p95 for latency-sensitive paths. If it balloons we fallback to cached verification. Document fallback policy.

maria: Backwards compat: we keep existing API keys live until conversion; we will tag legacy keys as "legacy" and surface them in Console with a deprecation banner. Migration window: 90 days opt-in, then enforced for new orgs.

alex: Policy enforcement nuance: if a resource belongs to org A but the broker-issued token references project B, we must reject. Enforce resource->org binding in minting layer.

nathan: Also need to consider cross-account delegation for partner integrations. That should be a separate workflow with explicit consent flow + audit.

kelly: For Dedicated/Private customers who self-manage, default to vault-ref approach. We'll provide operator broker as an optional component they can deploy.

jordan: Security review checklist: threat model for broker (privilege escalation, replay, forging), KMS ACLs, revocation/rotation testing, telemetry injection points.

siva: Implementation tasks (short): 1) auth-broker prototype + JWT signing keys 2) revocation service + API 3) Console UX to show token bindings 4) migration CLI 5) tests and perf benchmarks.

maria: Decision call: consensus to build broker + vault-ref support, staged rollout as described. Action items: Jordan to own broker design doc, Siva to own revocation and perf tests, Alex to draft migration CLI, Kelly to own Console UX + customer comms.

jordan: I'll put a detailed design PR up by EOD Friday and include threat model notes.

siva: I'll add perf harness and try to baseline mint path < 5ms p95.

kelly: Customer comms draft: short note explaining benefits + migration timeline + contact for assistance. I'll share tomorrow.

maria: Good. Also add a telemetry event when migration starts/completes: `auth.migration.run` with org_id, before_count, after_count.

nathan: tiny nit: consider allowing org admins to extend token TTL for specific service types (e.g. long-running analytics) — but require a justification field in Console and an auditable approval log.

jordan: That can be a policy knob; default deny, allow via admin approval. We'll add it to the design doc.

maria: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll update the RFC with the selected path and the action owners. :thumbsup:

kelly: no objections from me. :+1:

jordan: same.

siva: ack

ops-bot: incident-bot: NOTE: new alert rule "Auth Broker Errors > 5%" created in staging for canary.

maria: leaving this thread open for any additional comments, but proceeding to write the design PR.
